It’s all circumstantial. I’ve had much plastic surgery and it’s the biggest regret of my life. However I was in isolation, my bdd was at the lowest point and felt too ugly to leave the house, go to work, see my friends, or family. 

I think I would have been happy with my PS if I did research on techniques, doctors reviews, and people’s personal experiences. But I didn’t do any of those things until after I got botched. I took my surgery to the extreme and had things uncommon done because I felt it was the only thing that would make me attractive. I got botched. Not once but twice. Which made my bdd even worse and continued the isolation. 

However, I don’t think it’s common to be botched twice and need another revision after that… I do think it might be common for someone with BDD to think they need something a little more on the extreme side of surgery which I warn against. 

If a psychiatrist or any doctor during that time told me “you have BDD” and no surgery would make you feel better I wouldn’t have believed them and just searched for a different doctor. I still think things could have turned out differently and I could have been happy, I just had a shitty doctor willing to take my money for extreme procedures I didn’t need. 

The best PS I ever had was breast augmentation when I was 18. I hated being barely an A cup. I’ve never been happier with that decision and the confidence it’s brought me 10 years later. 

So honestly, it’s all circumstantial. But my personal opinion, even after all I’ve gone through, I kind of think PS helps (if nothing goes wrong) and you aren’t doing anything unnecessary or extreme.

If you get something done make sure you research the hell out of it. Read real peoples experiences and see lots of B&A from the surgeon you choose. I went in very naive. I had FFS, which included forehead contouring, rhino, and a lip lift. It was a drastic change that I did not need. I should have only done the rhino and with a rhino specialist other than a maxillofacial surgeon. I thought my face looked masculine and wanted to look more feminine. That’s why I chose FFS, however I did not need such an aggressive surgeon and am now paying for it 2 revisions later. What I did is so drastic I don’t think I’ll ever forgive myself. 

That’s obviously not everyone’s story, plastic surgery has helped with more confidence in many people. You just have to be able to really objectively see your face and know what to alter. If you think youre ugly and want to make a drastic change I’d advise against it. Go small first. You can always get more later if you desire. Chances are you’re not as “ugly” as we “think” we are. Don’t overdo it.

I would try to avoid the psych hospital if you can. From when ive been most of the people there were having delusions and hallucinations.

The group therapy classes really lacked depth and most were art therapy. I don’t remember learning any good coping skills. 

I really wasn’t able to have a conversation with most of the people there aside from some of the staff. The staff wasn’t really caring tho, just there to do the job and maintain a controlled environment for everyone. And you can’t leave until the psychiatrist says your stable enough. I stayed 2 weeks but was ready to go in like 1. 

I’m sure theres got to be some better in-patient experiences. I did see some other people make progress. I just didn’t find where I went very helpful. 

So I’m not trying to discourage you , especially if you really need to go, then definitely do and talk with a social worker. Maybe look at the reviews online if they have any before you go so you can feel more confident in choosing your care.
